Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call:

- You confirmed Acme's primary concerns are PII handling, data retention lengths for inference logs, and an explicit opt-out for any use of your production data for model training or improvement.
- Action items for Redwood: provide a written confirmation of the training opt-out, clarify logging/retention behavior, and share the DPA amendment for procurement.

Per the conversation, here are the key points we discussed and what we'll deliver:

1) Training opt-out: We can confirm that, upon signature of the attached opt-out form and execution of the DPA amendment, Redwood will not use Acme production request/response data to train or improve our models. That includes excluding your inference logs from any training datasets or internal model evaluation pipelines.

2) Logging & retention: By default, inference request logs are retained for 30 days for debugging and billing. We can provide options to reduce retention windows or route logs to your S3 bucket with a lifecycle policy. Audit logs (who accessed what) are retained for 12 months by default; we can extend that as a paid add-on if needed.

3) Data residency: Your production instances on our Dedicated plan can be pinned to the us-east-1 region. Data stored for billing/metrics will remain in US regions per your requirement.

Please review the attached opt-out form (redwood-training-opt-out-form.pdf) and the proposed DPA amendment (updated-dpa-acmeinc-20260218.pdf). Once signed, we will update your account flags to ensure data is excluded from any model training workflows and confirm in writing.

Next steps:
- I can send the DocuSign link for both documents if that works for procurement.
- If security wants more technical detail, Aditya is copied and can provide a short write-up of the logging pipeline and how we filter data for training.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick call with your security team if helpful.

Best,

Kimberly Park
